title: Chat-bridge: OpenAI ChatCompletions polymorphic request/response mapper with streaming & function-call fidelity
creator: Asha Gupta
description: Implement a compatibility mapper that accepts OpenAI ChatCompletions-style HTTP requests and produces Redwood-internal request shapes, and vice-versa for responses. This ticket focuses on three fidelity requirements: 1) streaming semantics (token-level and function-call event streaming), 2) exact function/tool-calling behavior (name/arguments/finish/retry semantics), and 3) structured output (JSON schema validation and partial-JSON streaming). The mapper must be tolerant of common client deviations (timestamped messages, system/meta fields, mixed role naming), preserve idempotency and message ordering, and emit telemetry that lets Console trace request <-> model output mappings. The component will live in the ingress compat layer as a lightweight, stateless translator service that can be attached to both Hosted API and Dedicated gateways.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming OpenAI ChatCompletions JSON (messages + functions + stream=true) is transformed into Redwood request envelope with preserved message ordering and role mapping
Streaming tokens are emitted as Redwood streaming events that include token text, token_id (sequence index), and stream_fragment_id for reassembly
Function call invocation is surfaced as a first-class event with name, raw args (string), and parsed args where parsable; finish events include returned value and an explicit 'completed' flag

If client requests structured response schema (JSON Schema in user properties), partial JSON fragments are validated incrementally and malformed fragments trigger circuiter but non-fatal 'schema_regression' events
Compatibility mapper passes automated conformance tests against the OA ChatCompletions golden test suite (10k permutations) with >=99.7% fidelity margin for request/response shape and streaming order
Telemetry links per-request include original OA request body, normalized Redwood envelope id, and mapping deltas
No customer-requested API keys or secrets are recorded in logs; PII redaction applied per security guidelines
plan: Design mapping spec (messages -> segments; role mapping table; functions contract) — docs/confluence/compat-mapper-design
Implement core transformer library (pure functions) in rust -> wasm for gateway embedding
Integrate transformer into ingress adapter with streaming parser that emits tokenized fragments
Add function-call emitter that creates a deterministic 'tool_invocation' event and captures back-channel results
Write conformance tests (sync, streaming, mid-stream tool-call, schema-violation) and run against internal harness
Canary deploy to Hosted API for 1% of traffic behind feature flag, monitor telemetry and errorbudget impact
Iterate on edge cases found in canary and broaden rollout
design_notes: We avoid modifying user payloads except to normalize role names (assistant/system/user -> assistant/system/user) and move non-standard metadata into 'x-rw-meta' to maintain parity

Streaming: use a two-layer chunking strategy: token_aware fragments (preserve token boundaries) and envelope fragments (for large tool responses). Each chunk carries a fragment id and offset to enable idempotent reassembly on the client side
Function calls: keep raw string args in 'raw_args' and attempt JSON parse into 'parsed_args' with deterministic fallback. If parse fails, set parse_error metadata but still forward raw_args
Structured output: when a JSON schema is supplied, run incremental validation (ajv-like streamed validator). On violation, emit 'schema_regression' event and attach failing fragment sample (redacted)
Performance: transformer must add <1ms median and <5ms p95 on top of existing ingress latency for non-streaming requests; streaming overhead budget is 5% of CPU for active connections
Security: mapper will never materialize KMS keys or decrypt content; it will flag if a request appears to be a key exchange and route to security review
risks: Edge-case function-call sequences where model emits interleaved tokens and partial function names could cause misattribution — mitigated by fragment reassembly rules
Incremental JSON validation could be expensive on long outputs -> fallback to sampling-based validation for very large payloads
Client expectations for OpenAI semantics (e.g., implicit truncation) differ; we may need an opt-in 'oa-strict' mode for parity with legacy clients
Telemetry volume: capturing original OA bodies for every request may blow up storage; we will sample 0.1% by default and keep full payloads only for errors
telemetry: Expose dashboards: Console -> Compatibility -> OA Mapper (latency, errors, per-model breakdown)
testing: Unit: transformer pure functions with property-based tests for role/name permutations
Integration: harness that replays OA golden data (10k permutations) and asserts message ordering and tool-call sequences
Load: simulate 50k concurrent streaming connections to ensure CPU + memory budgets hold
Security: fuzz OA request shapes to detect header/body injection and ensure no secrets logged
Acceptance: run CI conformance job that mirrors production canary traffic pattern
rollout: Feature flag gating: rc.oa_compat_mapper; default off
Canary: 1% traffic for 72 hours, monitor mapping error rate and Console dashboards
Expand: 10% for 48 hours if metrics stable, then to 50% for 24 hours, then full roll
Fallback: automatic disable if error rate spike > 5x baseline or p95 latency regression > 20%
Docs: publish migration guide for customers who rely on OA legacy quirks and provide oa-strict toggle
